claim: The EU Migration Pact forces the Baltic states to accept migrants from other EU countries
claimed_by: Populist politicians and social media posts in the Baltic states
conflict: The Pact lets each country choose between taking people, paying or giving other support; Latvia and Lithuania have said they will not take relocated migrants, and fewer than 1,000 people are expected to be relocated across the whole EU in 2026.
verdict_note: The rules and the published pledges contradict it.

claim: Latvia will have to take 10,000 migrants a year or pay 200 million euros
claimed_by: Latvian populist politicians before the 2024 European elections (fact-checked by Re:Baltica)
conflict: Re:Baltica found the estimate for Latvia at the time was 99 people or 2 million euros; the agreed 2026 pool for the whole EU is 21,000 relocations or equivalent support.
verdict_note: An older claim that still circulates; the figures were wrong by about a hundred times.

claim: Belarusian border officials help organise illegal migration into Latvia
claimed_by: Latvian prosecutors
conflict: Belarus has not responded to this specific case; the evidence comes from an ongoing criminal investigation.
verdict_note: Consistent with documented state organisation of migration from Belarus since 2021, but not yet tested in court.

claim: Migrants are forced to damage Latvian border equipment if they cannot pay smugglers
claimed_by: Latvian prosecutors; LTV De facto
conflict: Based on testimony gathered in an ongoing investigation; no independent confirmation yet.
verdict_note: Credible and specific, but still under investigation.

claim: The EU Migration Pact forces the Baltic states to accept migrants from other EU countries
claimed_by: Populist politicians and social media posts in the Baltic states
conflict: New: Lithuania is moving from taking a small group to paying only, which the rules allow; each country chooses between taking people, paying or other support.
verdict_note: The rules and Lithuania's own choices contradict it.

claim: Lithuania will not accept a single migrant under the EU solidarity mechanism
claimed_by: Lithuanian Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas
conflict: The government has not yet approved the proposal, and Lithuania agreed in May to take 58 people from Cyprus; it is unclear whether that pledge is cancelled.
verdict_note: Backed by a government commission, but not final.

claim: Saboteurs and hundreds of illegal migrants have entered Estonia through Latvia
claimed_by: EKRE chairman Martin Helme; Centre Party chairman Mihhail Kõlvart
conflict: The Threod suspects were residents of Latvia; Estonian police detained 149 people for illegal migration in the first half of 2026, many believed to have come via Latvia. The government says this does not justify border checks.
verdict_note: Broadly matches police figures and the Threod case, but no full-year figure for arrivals via Latvia has been published.

claim: Russia may push migrants toward Estonia's border once the road crossings close
claimed_by: Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal
conflict: No migrant movement toward the Estonian border has been reported; the precedent is Russia's 2023 push at the Finnish border.
verdict_note: A reasonable contingency warning, not evidence of a planned push.

claim: The EU Migration Pact forces the Baltic states to accept migrants from other EU countries
claimed_by: Populist politicians and social media posts in the Baltic states; not newly spread today
conflict: Lithuania's interior minister again said on 18 November that member states may choose to accept people or pay instead, and Lithuania is choosing to pay; Estonia and Poland are exempt from contributing.
verdict_note: The Pact lets each state choose relocation, payment or other support; no Baltic state is required to take anyone.

claim: Lithuania will not accept a single migrant under the EU solidarity mechanism next year
claimed_by: Lithuanian Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas
conflict: The minister repeated the plan on 18 November; a government commission approved it, but formal government approval and the payment amount have not been reported.
verdict_note: Stated on the record twice this week; still awaiting a formal government decision.

claim: Paying into the EU solidarity pool is cheaper for Lithuania than accepting relocated migrants
claimed_by: Lithuanian Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas, citing an estimate over about five years
conflict: No calculation has been published and the payment amount is not yet set; this year Lithuania combined both, agreeing to take 58 people and pay €1.4 million.
verdict_note: A plausible on-the-record estimate that cannot be checked until the figures are published.

claim: Restoring checks on Estonia's border with Latvia would cost about €65 million
claimed_by: Estonian Interior Ministry secretary general Tarmo Miilits (18 November)
conflict: Earlier in the week a figure of roughly €300 million was reported in the Estonian debate; neither estimate says whether it is one-off or annual or what it includes.
verdict_note: Both figures come from Estonian officials, but the published estimates do not match and have not been explained.

claim: Russia may push migrants toward Estonia's border once the road crossings close
claimed_by: Estonian officials and security agencies
conflict: Estonia's interior ministry says agencies are prepared for such retaliation; no movement of migrants toward the Estonian border has been reported, and Russia has not commented.
verdict_note: A contingency Estonia is planning for, in line with Finland's 2023 experience, not an observed event.

claim: The EU Migration Pact forces the Baltic states to accept migrants from other EU countries
claimed_by: Populist politicians and social media posts in the Baltic states; not newly spread today
conflict: The Pact lets states relocate people, pay or offer other support. Lithuania is choosing to pay, and the Commission's designations give the Baltic states priority access to support rather than new obligations.
verdict_note: No Baltic state is required to take anyone.

claim: Poland and Estonia are exempt from contributing to the EU solidarity pool
claimed_by: LRT/BNS reporting on Lithuania's solidarity choice; repeated in our 19 November edition
conflict: The Commission lists Poland and Estonia among six states facing a significant migratory situation, which allows them to request full or partial deductions; the Council has not yet decided for 2027.
verdict_note: An exemption is possible but not yet decided; 'may request deductions' is the accurate wording.

claim: Paying into the EU solidarity pool is cheaper for Lithuania than accepting relocated migrants
claimed_by: Lithuania's interior minister
conflict: Paying costs €20,000 per person not relocated under the Pact's reference figure; the ministry has published no estimate of the cost of hosting relocated people over five years.
verdict_note: Plausible but no figures have been published.

claim: Latvia's 2026 crossing attempts have already exceeded the whole of 2025
claimed_by: Latvia's State Border Guard
conflict: About 13,012 prevented attempts by 16 November against 12,046 in 2025; officials say the same people may be counted more than once.
verdict_note: True as a count of attempts; it does not mean more people crossed or tried to cross.

claim: Russia may push migrants toward Estonia's border once the road crossings close
claimed_by: Estonian interior ministry, as a contingency
conflict: No unusual movement has been reported on the Russian side of the border.
verdict_note: A precautionary scenario, not an observed trend.

claim: The EU Migration Pact forces the Baltic states to accept migrants from other EU countries
claimed_by: Populist politicians and social media posts in the Baltic states; not newly spread today
conflict: The Pact lets states relocate people, pay or offer other support. Lithuania is choosing to pay, and the Commission's designations give the Baltic states priority access to support rather than new obligations.
verdict_note: No Baltic state is required to take anyone.

claim: Estonia has returned more than 400 migrants to Latvia this year
claimed_by: Our 20 November edition, summarising ERR reporting
conflict: ERR's 3 November report, citing police, gave 388 people found in Estonia this year and 148 handed back to Latvia. A later figure may be higher, but no source found gives over 400 returns.
verdict_note: The best available figure is about 150 returns; 'over 400' appears to count people caught, not returned.

claim: Poland and Estonia are exempt from contributing to the EU solidarity pool
claimed_by: LRT/BNS reporting on Lithuania's solidarity choice
conflict: The Commission lists Poland and Estonia among six states that may request full or partial deductions; the Council has not yet decided for 2027.
verdict_note: An exemption is possible but not yet decided.

claim: Russia may push migrants toward Estonia's border once the road crossings close
claimed_by: Estonian interior ministry, as a contingency
conflict: No unusual movement has been reported on the Russian side; Moscow's announced response is political and diplomatic.
verdict_note: A precautionary scenario, not an observed trend.
